concept: Text is the printing on the case of an appliance: one grotesk in two weights, grey ink flat on the plastic, with hierarchy told by size and by where the words sit on the unit.

default_to_avoid.pattern: generic typography text component with h1 to h6 variants and bold, italic and colour props (MUI Typography, Chakra Text)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A colour prop invites orange or tinted words, and bold or italic add voices that P5 forbids, since printing has two weights and one ink.

default_to_avoid.pattern: text with uppercase letter-spaced small labels as a house style
default_to_avoid.why_not: Spaced capitals turn every small label into a second voice and break the lowercase model name, which P5 keeps as the only case change.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): small grey grotesk printed along the inset lines of the case
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): one grotesk in two weights, numbers set on a fixed width
system/refs/ref-01.png: wordmark bottom-left and lowercase model name bottom-right (estimated from chat)

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only; hierarchy by size and position
derivation.form: Text exposes five size steps from type.micro to type.reading and a weight prop limited to regular and medium, with no bold or italic.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes; no tinted text
derivation.form: The tone prop picks text.primary or text.secondary only, both measured at 4.5:1 or more on surface.solid and surface.raised.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Text has no colour prop at all, so words can never be painted action.accent and the orange stays on the unit's one control.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The numeric prop switches on tabular figures so a changing number keeps its width and the line beside it never shifts.

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material — no shadow, no emboss
derivation.form: Text never carries text-shadow, outline or elevation tokens; it sits flat in the same plane as the plastic it is printed on.

variants.reason: A tells hierarchy only by size and position as P5 asks, keeps sentence case readable at every step, and leaves lowercase to the model name; B adds spaced capitals as a second voice and capitalises the model name, and C makes every label look like a model name so it can no longer identify anything.

root.why: Printing sits flat on the plastic with no outer margin, no shadow and the system grotesk.

micro.why: The smallest step prints the model name and scale numerals on the case, at 11px.

caption.why: Caption prints the wordmark and short notes under a part, one step above micro.

label.why: Label names a control or a reading beside it, at the same size as the word on a key.

body.why: Body carries a sentence or two inside a unit, with the leading set for short lines.

reading.why: Reading prose is capped at the measure so long lines never stretch across a sheet.

primary.why: Primary ink is the darkest grey on plastic and holds 4.5:1 or more in both themes.

secondary.why: Secondary ink is one step lighter for notes and units, and still holds 4.5:1 on plastic.

regular.why: Regular weight is the default for printing, so medium is left to name things.

medium.why: Medium weight marks a name or a label, the only heavier weight the grotesk is allowed.

numeric.why: Tabular figures keep a changing number at a fixed width so the line beside it stays put.
